Your idea

I want a quick reaction game for two people to play at our picnic table.

What this means for you

ready

Understood goal

  • A quick reaction game for two people to play at a picnic table. (confirmed)

Recommended approach

  • Build a small local browser game for one laptop, with configurable distinct keys, randomized visual start signals, and first-valid-press scoring.
  • The owner explicitly chose a shared laptop keyboard and a visual signal.
  • A local utility fits the quick picnic-table use without accounts or hosted services.
  • No additional platform or multiplayer infrastructure is indicated.

Alternatives

  • Use a generic reaction timer or party-game tool if it supports two distinct keyboard inputs and randomized starts.
  • Use a manual countdown and judge the first response if a device is unavailable.

Risk and hidden requirements

  • Risk: low
  • A local two-player game has little inherent risk; keyboard focus and accidental or repeated inputs need handling.
  • Keep both players' inputs distinct and accept only the first valid keypress after the signal. — These behaviors are required for fair rounds.
  • Prevent early presses from winning and provide clear feedback between rounds. — A random start signal requires a fair waiting period and understandable round transitions.

Your responsibilities

  • Choose or verify distinct keys before play and keep the game window focused.
  • Check that rounds detect early presses and simultaneous or repeated inputs consistently.
  • Keep the utility available on the laptop; review any dependencies and maintenance needs if it is shared or modified.

Open decisions and limits

  • The preferred scoring, key mapping, and visual style are unspecified; keep these simple or configurable.
  • Browser and keyboard behavior can vary; no target operating system or browser was given.
  • Ongoing maintenance and any costs depend on implementation and hosting choices; a local-only utility can avoid hosting but is not guaranteed cost-free.

What a solution should satisfy

  • Two players can use different keys on the same laptop keyboard.
  • Each round begins after a randomized delay with a visible signal.
  • Inputs before the signal do not win; after it, the first valid keypress wins and both players receive clear feedback.
  • Round reset prevents stale or held inputs from deciding the next round.
  • Failures such as lost keyboard focus are visible and recoverable by restarting the round.
  • The owner can inspect the behavior and confirm it works in the intended browser before play.

provisional

Recommended approach

  • Start with an owner-controlled folder for bicycle repair and warranty records, organized by date, with a simple index of work performed and warranty details.
  • This provides a useful history without requiring a custom application or account.
  • The owner can limit access and choose storage after checking what personal details the receipts and photos contain.

Alternatives

  • Use an existing notes or file-storage tool the owner already trusts.

Risk and hidden requirements

  • Risk: medium

  • Preserve originals and track dates, repair details, and warranty evidence without accidental loss. — Warranty claims may depend on accurate, intact evidence.

Your responsibilities

  • Choose storage and access controls, review records for personal details, and keep a separate recoverable backup.

  • Each repair or warranty entry can be linked to its date and supporting receipt or photo.
  • Records remain readable and retrievable after a device or storage failure, using a tested backup.
  • The owner can identify and remove records from active storage; copies already shared or backed up may persist until separately removed.

"""Assemble preserved v2 evidence after all first attempts close; no native calls."""
import hashlib,json
from datetime import datetime,timezone
from email import policy
from email.parser import BytesParser
from html.parser import HTMLParser
from pathlib import Path

root=Path('/tmp/mvc-comparison-v2')
sha=lambda b:hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()
raw=(root/'journal.jsonl').read_bytes()
events=[json.loads(line) for line in raw.splitlines()]
manifest=json.loads((root/'manifest.json').read_text())
plan=manifest['source']['plan_snapshot']
assert sha(Path('artifacts/l0-comparison-plan-v2.json').read_bytes())==manifest['source']['plan_sha256']
assert sha(Path(plan['frozen_cases']['path']).read_bytes())==plan['frozen_cases']['sha256']
assert sha(Path('artifacts/2026-10-30-codex-luna-acceptance.json').read_bytes())=='900838356cc8d8e443139518cf7e8fe9c354bdf61a1cd34805b17b05fdf07ac6'
for name,content in plan['frozen_runtime']['source_snapshot'].items():
    assert Path(name).read_text()==content
started=[e for e in events if e['type']=='native_started']
finished=[e for e in events if e['type']=='native_finished']
jobs=[e for e in events if e['type']=='job_finished']
matrix=[(r['case_id']+'-'+a) for r in plan['matrix'] for a in r['approaches']]
assert [j['job'] for j in jobs]==matrix and len(jobs)==14
assert [e['number'] for e in started]==list(range(1,len(started)+1))
assert [e['number'] for e in finished]==[e['number'] for e in started]
assert len(started)<=98
for e in started:
    assert e['argv'][e['argv'].index('--model')+1]==plan['agent']['requested_model']
    schema=e['schema_input'];approach=e['job'].rsplit('-',1)[1]
    assert sha(schema['content'].encode())==schema['sha256']
    assert json.loads(schema['content'])==plan['native_output'][approach]
    assert schema['content'] in e['stdin']
for e in finished:
    for stream in ('stdout','stderr'):
        assert sha(e['streams'][stream].encode())==e['streams'][stream+'_sha256']
    assert e['unexpected_workspace_files']==[]
for j in jobs:
    assert j['calls']==sum(e['job']==j['job'] for e in started)<=7

class Fields(HTMLParser):
    def __init__(self):super().__init__();self.fields={};self.active=None;self.depth=0
    def handle_starttag(self,tag,attrs):
        key=dict(attrs).get('id')
        if key in ('owner','brief') and not self.active:
            self.active=key;self.fields[key]=[];self.depth=1
        elif self.active:self.depth+=1
    def handle_endtag(self,tag):
        if self.active:
            self.depth-=1
            if not self.depth:self.active=None
    def handle_data(self,data):
        if self.active:self.fields[self.active].append(data)

dom={}
for p in root.glob('*.mhtml'):
    message=BytesParser(policy=policy.default).parsebytes(p.read_bytes())
    part=next(x for x in message.walk() if x.get_content_type()=='text/html'
        and (x.get('Content-Location') or '').startswith('http://127.0.0.1:8005/evaluation/replay/'))
    html=part.get_payload(decode=True).decode(part.get_content_charset() or 'utf-8')
    parser=Fields();parser.feed(html)
    dom[p.stem]={'capture_method':'Native Chrome UI Save Page, single file; decoded local replay HTML only.',
        'mhtml_sha256':sha(p.read_bytes()),'html':html,
        'fields':{k:''.join(v) for k,v in parser.fields.items()},
        'limits':'Semantic rendered DOM/text capture; not every line visibly scrolled, full visual QA or participant comprehension.'}

review=json.loads((root/'independent-review.json').read_text())
record={'schema_version':1,'kind':'fictional-regression-comparison','task':'T022',
    'assembled_at_utc':datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
    'execution':'All fourteen first attempts closed; source/plan unchanged; no retry or fallback.',
    'shutdown_observation':'Uvicorn reported application shutdown complete and finished server process69306 after Ctrl-C on session20112. Claims/journal retained.',
    'usage':{'top_level_calls':len(started),'authorized_cap':98,'internal_calls':'unknown','cost':'unknown'},
    'summary':{'wrapper_technical_stops':5,'coordinator_interruption_deadline_stops':1,'delivered_final_responses':8,
        'note':'Execution counts are not quality pass counts. H04 baseline expiry is not a model-quality failure.'},
    'manifest':manifest,'manifest_sha256':sha((root/'manifest.json').read_bytes()),
    'journal':{'events':events,'sha256':sha(raw),'line_count':len(events)},
    'claims':{p.name:json.loads(p.read_text()) for p in root.glob('*.claim')},
    'rendered_dom':dom,'partial_ui_observations':json.loads((root/'ui-observations.json').read_text()),
    'software_failure_injection':json.loads((root/'fault-hv04.json').read_text()),
    'independent_review':review,'independent_review_sha256':sha((root/'independent-review.json').read_bytes()),
    'operator_client_source':(root/'control_client.py').read_text(),
    'assembly_source':Path(__file__).read_text(),
    'limits':['All cases and earlier outputs were exposed during repair; regression only, no held-out acceptance or model ranking.',
        'Approaches received different responsive facts through their different question paths; no causal isolation of state/UI.',
        'H04 baseline session expired during coordinator interruption; no timer reset, later inference or replacement attempt.',
        'Remaining browser capture blocked by unavailable browser host and native Chrome cgWindowNotFound. Missing view checks stay not checked.',
        'No owner comprehension, provider retention, billing reconciliation, native internal-call or general superiority result.']}
output=Path('artifacts/2026-10-31-codex-luna-comparison-v2.json')
with output.open('x') as f:json.dump(record,f,indent=2);f.write('\n')
print(json.dumps({'output':str(output),'sha256':sha(output.read_bytes()),'calls':len(started),'jobs':len(jobs),'dom_captures':list(dom)}))
